state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The misconception here is that changing all values by the same proportion would not affect the range. In fact, changing the values by the same proportion would change the range. Let's walk through the steps together to see why the range would change if the plants were cut in half or grew by 3 cm each.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so you're saying the range would change in both cases? But I thought if you cut them all in half, like divide by 2, that wouldn't change the range because you're doing the same thing to all of them... Can you show me what happens to the range when we actually work it out?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Student, the misconception here is that changing all values by the same proportion will not affect the range. Remember, the range is determined by the difference between the highest and lowest values in a set of data. Let's calculate the new range when the plants are cut in half and when they grow by 3 cm each to see how it changes.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Yeah okay, so like... can you actually show me the numbers? Like what's the range before and after we cut them in half? Because I'm still confused about why dividing everything by 2 would change the range if we're doing the same thing to all of them.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher repeatedly states the misconception without engaging with the student's reasoning, refuses to show calculations despite direct requests, provides no scaffolding for the student to discover why proportional changes affect range, and the student shows no progress—remaining confused and asking the same question by Turn 4.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher repeatedly states conceptual claims about proportions and range without providing any explicit procedures, worked steps with actual calculations, or direct corrective feedback on the specific numerical errors, despite the student explicitly requesting to see the actual numbers worked out.
